title: Preference Tuning: RLHF and DPO
summary: People find it easier to say which of two answers is better than to write the perfect one. Preference tuning turns those comparisons into training signal: a Bradley-Terry reward model plus reinforcement learning with a KL penalty (RLHF), or the same objective optimised directly on pairs (DPO). The lesson ends with RL on verifiable rewards and the ways all of these go wrong.
objectives: Explain why pairwise preferences are collected and how they fit into the post-training pipeline
Write the Bradley-Terry model P(y_w ≻ y_l) = σ(r_w − r_l) and compute the reward-model loss for a pair
Write the RLHF objective with a KL penalty and evaluate PPO's clipped objective for a sample
Derive the DPO loss from the KL-regularised objective and compute it for a pair of log-probabilities
Recognise reward hacking, length bias and over-optimisation and explain how β and evaluation guard against them
prerequisites: You should understand SFT and loss masking ([Instruction Tuning](/learn/training-and-adaptation/instruction-tuning)) and the log-probability of a sequence ([Next-Token Prediction and Sampling](/learn/model-foundations/sampling)). The sigmoid function and KL divergence are defined where they are used.
